apps.localizedDescription: A free and open-source PlayStation 2 (PS2) emulator based on PCSX2, with native ARM64 JIT recompilers. Play PS2 games on your phone, PC, or gaming handheld.

versions.localizedDescription:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- Android: regenerate the PGO profile on the source with the GS runs build
- tests: the block hasher's unaligned update stays inside the test memory
- GS: comments that named removed gsrunner switches, and an include they needed
- GS/Vulkan: the run machine's development log goes
- GS/TC: the lean path's mode switch and check halves go
- gsrunner: the burst memo's switches and statistics line go
- gsrunner: the readback lane's statistics, trace and switches go
- gsrunner: the kick's two check modes go
- GS/Vulkan: the run machine sleeps where runs do not form
- GS: the vertex buffer grows in 64-bit sizes and fails loudly past a ceiling
- GS: a reset of the draw buffers frees the buffers it replaces
- GS/SW: a draw whose frame and Z buffers share pages is not split between workers
- GS/SW: a texture is not refilled while a queued draw still reads it
- GS/Vulkan: a run that holds a large draw keeps one state for all its draws
- GS/Vulkan: a draw that cannot open a run is primed before it is classified
- GS/Vulkan: the stencil counter resolve pipeline takes blend constants and line width dynamic
- GS/Vulkan: the run pipeline declares its dynamic state through AddCachedDynamicState
- GS/Vulkan: the stencil counter resolve pipeline takes blend constants and line width dynamic
- GS/Vulkan: a run opens at the second of two consecutive draws that share its fixed state
- GS/Vulkan: a draw with a vertex-selector bit runs never take is refused first, with the pixel-shader check
- gsrunner: -kick-convert-check runs the kick's old conversion pass beside the new one
- GS: the kick kernel converts a job in stretches, with nothing tested per vertex
- GS/Vulkan: the stencil counter resolve pipeline keeps blend constants and line width dynamic
- GS/Vulkan: the run machine's rings are made by the first draw that would join a run
- GS/Vulkan: a draw that continues a run still counts toward the readback in-pass kick
- gsrunner: -kick-decide-check runs the kick's wide decision beside the four-wide one
- GS: the kick kernel decides on raw 16-bit coordinates, both axes in one lane
- tests: block identities over held depth words are those of the words
- GS: choose the block identity by timing the candidates once, on the first use
- GS/HW: keep the palette's hash while the renderer's palette has not been rewritten
- GS/CLUT: the palette's alpha range with one LD4 per 16 entries on ARM64
- tests: pin the alpha range of an expanded palette
- GS/HW: take a level's block identities in one call, and combine them with AES
- GS/HW: a CPU clear of whole pages gives their blocks the identity of what it wrote
- GS/HW: key every texture lookup that names nothing by the identities of its blocks
- GS: GSBlockId, a cheaper identity for a block of local memory inside one run
- tests: pin the texture hashes that name dumped and replacement textures
- gsrunner: the run machine keeps -runs on|off and -runs-log; the probing switches go
- GS/Vulkan: a draw outside the run program's pixel-shader set is refused first, for two masks
- GS/Vulkan: declining the targets whose runs do not pay (off, unfinished)
- GS/Vulkan: draws that alternate two sets of constants reuse the earlier upload
- gsrunner: -runs-nofill-classic, the classic path's no-fill arm (development)
- GS/Vulkan: the dear split weighs fill against a host draw, per GPU class
- tests: a hand-worked case of the kick kernel's four-wide decision
- gsrunner: the readback lane's measurement scaffolding
- MTGS: a GS-to-EE read spins only while spinning has been answering it
- MTGS: a GS-to-EE read spins for its answer, and the GS thread for the next read
- GS/Vulkan: the in-pass kick spends at most a quarter of the readback wait it saves
- GS/Vulkan: after the gate refuses an in-pass kick, offer it again 32 draws later
- GS/Vulkan: in a readback frame the kick also ends a pass of many draws
- GS/HW: the depth target holds the moved words until local memory is read or written there
- GS/Vulkan: the run log carries each run's bounding-box area by dear class (development)
- GS/HW: a Z24 move of colour pages into a depth target stays on the GPU
- GS: a whole-page Z24 move of colour pages lands as a fixed block permutation
- GS/HW: a burst's second read comes from its first round trip
- GS/HW: the target reads of one request share one GPU round trip
- GS/Vulkan: a run flushed from inside an apply keeps the classic path's chosen pipeline
- GS: a new draw's first vertices are replayed only where a flush check is asked
- GS: the kernel's conversion pass stands behind its own interface
- gsrunner: -runs-no-continue, to price the run machine's shortcut (development)
- GS/Vulkan: the run log records which fixed state ended a run (development)
- GS/Vulkan: additive draws join runs
- GS/Vulkan: recorded keys with raster ordering or a stencil counter are loadable
- GS: the kernel's driver takes the per-draw environment snapshot itself
- tests: every recorded pipeline key a draw can make is loadable
- GS: the kick kernel decides a chunk first and converts only the vertices that stay
- GS/HW: the CPU memory clear's 24-bit and masked fills keep the old bits with one bit select
- GS: the burst memo uses GSClut's read serial
- GS/Vulkan: draws without a depth buffer and expanded sprites join runs
- GS/Vulkan: the run's header and table set takes a descriptor pool of its own
- GS/Vulkan: a game's recorded pipeline keys survive every build that keeps the key layout
- GS cache: a key layout identity, hashed from the pipeline selector definitions alone
- Android: a new install removes only the GPU caches older builds wrote
- Android: save the shader caches on every trip to the background, not once per 120 s
- GS cache: write a change a few seconds after it settles, not only every 30 s
- GS/Vulkan: on Android, name the linked GLSL compiler by its own versions
- GS/Vulkan: the driver's pipeline blob is stamped by the driver, not the app's build
- GS/Vulkan: every game's SPIR-V goes into the device's pack as well
- GS/Vulkan: warm the GLSL compiler on the compile queue when the device opens
- GS/Vulkan: the recorded-key precompile runs on GSCompileQueue
- GS: GSCompileQueue, a worker pool for shader and pipeline builds
- GS cache: a pack makes its directory again when its file is not there
- tests: a pack is written after its empty directory was removed
- GS/TC: a target keeps the end block of its valid area
- GS/HW: the burst memo rests through runs of block copies
- GS/HW: three values of Draw() are worked out only where they are read
- GS/HW: the burst memo leaves alone what the copy road cannot take at level 0
- GS/TC: the post-draw invalidation returns when no source is under the write
- GS/TC: the target lookup answers from the front of its list
- GS/HW: the burst memo prefetches what the next packet compare reads
- GS/HW: the burst memo invalidates the texture cache once per burst
- GS/HW: the burst memo tests its block-copy gate first
- gsrunner: the burst memo's vertex counts and slab footprint
- GS/HW: the burst memo records into recycled slabs
- GS: the burst memo has no setting
- gsrunner: -runs-split-mask, and the run log's per-state change counts
- GS/Vulkan: a draw that opens a run after a ring or texture-array end needs its program built too
- GS/Vulkan: the run machine's log counts its refusals by detail
- GS/Vulkan: a draw that continues a run skips the classic path's device work
- gsrunner: the run machine's development switches

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261108...22b1a7661fa5b29b54fd310911f16841d672bc6d
